items.title: Westwater Resources announces $25 million loan to advance Kellyton graphite plant
items.summary: Westwater Resources secured a $25 million direct loan from the Export-Import Bank of the United States (EXIM) to further develop its Kellyton graphite plant in Alabama. This funding, part of EXIM's Make More in America Initiative, will support construction, equipment installation, commissioning, and operational readiness, aiming for commercial production by 2027. The project is crucial for establishing a domestic supply chain for battery-grade natural graphite, reducing U.S. reliance on foreign sources for this critical mineral.

items.title: Transocean Share Surge Narrows Gap to Analyst Consensus View
items.summary: Transocean (NYSE:RIG) shares gained 0.7% on Friday, closing at $5.76, despite underperforming the broader S&P 500 energy sector. The stock's current price is 11.2% below the analyst consensus target of $6.40, indicating a narrowing gap. The company's proposed acquisition of Valaris Ltd. (NYSE:VAL) and recent oil price increases are key factors influencing its valuation and future prospects.

items.title: GM to Halt Chevrolet Sales in China, Ford Shifts Lincoln Output to US
items.summary: General Motors is ending Chevrolet sales in China after a significant decline in units over the past decade, choosing instead to focus on its Buick and Cadillac brands within the country. Concurrently, Ford will cease producing Lincoln vehicles in China for the U.S. market by 2030, citing tariffs and connected-vehicle regulations as key factors, and will shift to domestic manufacturing. These moves highlight the diminishing influence of U.S. automakers in China, as domestic brands like BYD and Geely increasingly dominate the market.

items.title: Carol Devine Miller sells stocks in Pfizer, Quest Diagnostics, Target, and U.S. Bancorp
items.summary: Representative Carol Devine Miller sold stocks in Pfizer, Quest Diagnostics, Target, and U.S. Bancorp through her United Bank Brokerage Account. These transactions, valued between $15,001 and $50,000 each, occurred on March 10, 2025, and were disclosed as part of her congressional transparency requirements. The sales reflect her personal investment strategy rather than an assessment of the companies' performance.

items.title: Ford and GM Are Locked in a New Battle Over Who’s the Most American Carmaker
items.summary: Ford and General Motors are engaged in a new rivalry, vying to be seen as the most American carmaker amidst the ongoing U.S. trade war. This struggle involves tariffs on imports and batteries, forcing the Detroit giants to compete on who is more crucial to the U.S. economy, despite previously attempting a united front against chaotic trade policies.

items.title: HSBC Stock And 2 Global Bank Picks for Trade and Rate Rule Changes
items.summary: This article identifies three global banking stocks—Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria (BBVA), Banco Santander (SAN), and HSBC Holdings (HSBA)—that are well-positioned to navigate the evolving landscape of trade, interest rates, and compliance regulations. These banks offer diversified operations, significant digital banking investments, and varying risk-reward profiles due to their exposure to emerging markets and credit quality considerations. The analysis emphasizes that careful stock selection is crucial as policy changes can rapidly shift market leadership.

items.title: Intuit Stock Is Up 7,369% Since Its 1993 IPO and It’s Down 45% This Year. Here’s the Fuller Picture.
items.summary: Intuit stock (INTU) has experienced a significant 45% drop in 2026, primarily due to intensifying AI-driven tax competition, despite a long-term gain of 7,369% since its 1993 IPO. While analysts have significantly cut their price targets, they still see an average 31% upside. TIKR’s model suggests an even higher valuation of $592 by 2030, implying a 71% total return, believing the market has overly discounted the AI threat compared to Intuit's underlying business strength.

items.title: Helix Acquisition Corp III Posts Q2 Profit on IPO Trust Interest
items.summary: Helix Acquisition Corp. III (Nasdaq: HLXC) reported a net income of $1.33 million for the second quarter of 2026, stemming from interest earned on its IPO trust account. The company, a SPAC, completed a $172.5 million IPO in January 2026 and now holds $175.05 million in its trust, reflecting a per-share value of $10.15. HLXC has until January 26, 2028, to complete a business combination, as it currently has no operations or revenue.
